history.dynasty: Unknown (described in sources as an 'ancient' temple; no builder or date documented)
history.summary: The Bhawani Amba Temple is an ancient Shakti shrine in Old Ambala City dedicated to Goddess Amba Devi (Bhawani Devi), a form of Durga. Multiple sources state that the name of the city Ambala is derived from the goddess's name; the sources describe the temple as 'of the ancient period' and 'there for a very long time', but no source gives a founding date or builder (verify). It is counted among Haryana's most sacred religious places and is a major pilgrimage centre drawing thousands of devotees; the temple is reported to provide free dharamshalas and free food/prasadam (verify). Minor address conflict: vushii lists 'Kumhar Mohalla Rd, Old Town, Ambala 134003' while the geocoder's POI match is 'Jagadhari Road, Ambala 133001'; earthtrip places it about 6 km west of Ambala Cantt Junction in Old Ambala City (verify). Coordinates are the geocoder POI match (30.34551, 76.83923).

town_description: Ambala is a historic city in northern Haryana, split into Ambala City and Ambala Cantonment, and one of India's busiest railway junctions. It is famous for its scientific-instruments industry and Air Force station.

visitor_information.best_time: Chaitra and Sharad Navratri (March/April and September/October) are the most festive periods.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM - 12:00 PM and 4:30 PM - 9:00 PM daily, continuous hours during Navratri (per earthtrip.in - verify). Photography prohibited inside the inner sanctum.
